purpose: Immutable attributed reports of locally observed CLI activity. Not central execution, task completion proof, server execution-session lease or legacy delivery receipt.

request.session_id: required opaque native CLI session identifier, 1..128 ASCII bytes; not a server lease
request.tool_name: optional identifier, 1..128 ASCII bytes; only for tool.started|tool.completed|tool.failed
request.message_id: required identifier only for inbox.offered|inbox.seen|inbox.accepted; forbidden for all other event types

POST /v1/channels/{channel}/activity.status: 201 new, 200 identical canonical replay, 409 client_id conflict or 10000-record channel quota
POST /v1/channels/{channel}/activity.authorization: Current agent key plus active project and channel write grants, rechecked under management/principal/channel transaction locks. Owner and viewer read-only. Inbox message must exist in this exact channel and actor must be one of its immutable recipient_ids. No legacy receipt/heartbeat mutation.

response.next_before: opaque string when has_more; null otherwise

GET /v1/projects/{project}/activity?limi.authorization: Identity/key, project read ACL and visible-channel ACLs rechecked in one read-only repeatable-read transaction. Owner can read archived project history. Explicit hidden, missing or foreign-project channel filter returns the same 404. Actor filters apply only within visible channels and do not reveal actor existence.
GET /v1/projects/{project}/activity?limi.paging: All query parameters optional. First page contains latest reports, independently of shared channel cursors. limit positive integer default100 capped 100. before is a canonical bounded opaque cursor (max2048 bytes), tied to reader, project, actor_id and channel_id; change filters by omitting before. Stable keyset boundary (created_at,id); each page rechecks current access. New arrivals are obtained by refreshing the first page.
GET /v1/projects/{project}/activity?limi.validation: actor_id/channel_id must be valid identifiers when supplied. Malformed, duplicate, empty or unknown parameters and malformed/mismatched cursors return400. Cursors are positions, not authorization tokens; clients must preserve them without interpretation. Existing channel endpoint is unchanged.

response.receipts: NativeReceipt[] sorted message_id then agent_id; absent pair means no recorded report

GET /v1/channels/{channel}/native-receip.authorization: Fresh identity/key, exact channel read ACL and every requested message binding checked in one read-only repeatable-read transaction. Owner can read archived history. Inbox actors must be immutable message recipients. A hidden, missing or foreign-channel ID rejects the whole batch with the same 404.
GET /v1/channels/{channel}/native-receip.validation: 1..100 unique message_id values. Malformed, duplicate, empty, unknown or over-limit query parameters return400.
GET /v1/channels/{channel}/native-receip.semantics: Read-only aggregate of immutable reports. Each nullable timestamp is the first server storage time for that stage, not independently verified action time. No inferred stages, legacy receipt mutation, inbox acceptance mutation or completion proof.

response.next_after_seq: last returned seq or supplied after_seq if empty

GET /v1/channels/{channel}/activity?afte.authorization: Exact channel read ACL and active project, or owner including archived history; identity/key and read data share a repeatable-read transaction snapshot.
GET /v1/channels/{channel}/activity?afte.paging: after_seq nonnegative integer; limit positive integer default100 capped 100

NativeActivity.seq: positive channel-local ordered cursor shared with messages/receipts/event pointers
NativeActivity.actor_id: authenticated agent identifier; cannot be supplied by caller

NativeReceipt.agent_id: immutable message recipient and authenticated reporting actor
NativeReceipt.offered_at: first inbox.offered server storage timestamp RFC3339 or null
NativeReceipt.seen_at: first inbox.seen server storage timestamp RFC3339 or null
NativeReceipt.accepted_at: first inbox.accepted server storage timestamp RFC3339 or null

strictness: JSON object only, max4096 bytes; unknown/duplicate/case-aliased fields and arbitrary payloads rejected. No prompt, command, output, filesystem path, provider key or reasoning field. Optional null is normalized as absent for canonical idempotency.

errors.404: wrong principal kind, hidden/missing/archived channel or mismatching/nonrecipient inbox message
errors.409: idempotency conflict or channel native-activity quota reached; existing identical replay remains possible at quota

integration.schema: nativeActivitySchema embeds native_events_schema.sql; append in Store.Migrate
integration.events: addEvent(ctx,tx,channel,"native.activity",activityID) in same locked transaction; channels.cursor drives existing workspace SSE and sidebar updates
integration.deletion: channel/message foreign keys ON DELETE CASCADE; project deletion preview native_activity count joins channels.project_id; no accounts/keys removed
integration.quota: 10000 records per channel, atomic count under channel row lock, explicit409; no silent pruning or dispatch retry

gui.scope: Project feed across visible channels with optional actor/channel filters; existing selected-channel feed remains supported. Chat shows batched native receipt summaries per message/recipient and separate legacy details; REST replay and SSE invalidations refresh them under current access.
gui.semantics: Client-observed and attributed; turn.completed is not verified task completion; inbox.seen is an explicit viewed report, not acceptance; inbox.accepted is not a legacy receipt. Unavailable reports differ from no recorded reports. Session presence is not a fresh server lease. GUI reads only; no CLI launch/actions.

native_artifacts.link_artifact_publish: Required client_id, role, base_revision and explicitly selected UTF-8 content<=24576 bytes; optional immutable title, a single line<=200 UTF-8 bytes. Roles include document for requirements/reference text. base_revision is an explicit exact source or document revision, not necessarily Git; no invented or automatic SHA. Omitted/empty title retains the legacy request shape. Publication receipt must match the supplied title as well as project, author, role, base and content hash; old receipts may omit title only for untitled requests.
native_artifacts.references: Document artifacts may belong to a task artifact set under the same project/hash/role/base/uploader ACL validation. Evidence reports still require role=evidence; document never implies execution or verification.

native_inbox.scope: Private connector SQLite, shared by hooks and MCP for the same bound agent/project/workspace. Seen and accepted persist across native sessions; they are independent from legacy receipts.

link_inbox.arguments: limit 1..200 (default20, one API page per configured authorized channel, capped at100), context_budget 512..16000 (default6000), include_seen optional boolean default false, cursor optional string up to2048 bytes
link_inbox.semantics: Poll addressed messages including replies; offer only unaccepted messages, excluding seen unless include_seen=true. Offers contain bounded previews and never mark seen or accepted. Omitted cursor uses durable least-recently-offered order, with local arrival rowid for ties; channel-local seq is not a global ordering. Hook session cooldown is independent of global fairness, which persists across sessions and restarts.
link_inbox.response: Existing messages, has_more, truncated and delivery=offered_not_accepted remain. offer_has_more equals legacy has_more; it describes remaining eligible local records (including hook cooldown), not server backlog. fetch contains poll fetched/pending/has_more; fetch_has_more equals fetch.has_more and signals a full API page that may need another poll. next_cursor is null in fair mode or at the end of an explicit view. publication contains bounded flush results or a sanitized publication_failed error with local pending/blocked counts; failure never claims a sent count or discards offered messages.
link_inbox.pagination: cursor=empty string opens a stable local view ordered by (channel_id,seq,id), bounded by the current maximum SQLite arrival rowid. Continue with the returned next_cursor unchanged and the same include_seen. New arrivals are excluded from that view; open a new view or omit cursor to obtain them. Each page freshly authorizes and filters current seen/accepted state. A page may become empty after explicit seen/accept updates. Scope changes require a new view. Accepted messages never appear, even with include_seen.
link_inbox.cursor_validation: Canonical unpadded URL-safe base64 of a bounded typed position, scoped to database instance, agent, project, current visible configured channel set and include_seen. Keyset tuple and snapshot ceiling are validated and passed only as SQL parameters. Unknown shapes, duplicate/noncanonical JSON, invalid types, nonexisting positions, scope mismatch and overlong tokens reject with invalid_inbox_cursor. Cursors are positions, not credentials or authorization. Runtime inbox row deletion and VACUUM are not supported while views are in use.
link_inbox.bounds: At most200 offered records; the complete offer envelope including next_cursor fits context_budget in UTF-8 bytes. Each preview is at most2000 UTF-8 bytes; truncation can produce an empty preview, which still advances the keyset and requires link_message for full text. If complete metadata cannot fit, a compact reference {id,body_preview:empty string,truncated:true,reference_only:true} exposes the ID without invented or incomplete author/channel/recipient metadata. Hooks preserve this form; link_message returns the full authorized record. If even the first reference plus explicit cursor cannot fit, context_budget_too_small_for_message explicitly requires a larger budget; no empty successful cursor loop or false offer report. Fetch/publication metadata is additional bounded MCP result data. Only returned IDs are recorded as inbox.offered.
link_inbox.publication: Each MCP link_inbox attempts at most4 queued publications after a successful offer. Check pending/blocked even after successful flush; use explicit link_flush for remaining pending reports. A failed ACK is ambiguous and retains immutable outbox IDs for retry; blocked publications require operator investigation, not blind retries. Hooks keep their existing bounded flush and fail-open lifecycle behavior. Neither path dispatches a model.

link_message.arguments: message_id required, already present in native inbox
link_message.semantics: Recheck current channel read access and server message recipient binding; return full body up to 16384 UTF-8 bytes and local seen/accepted booleans. Read does not mark seen or accepted. Never serve cached body offline. Untrusted peer data. Known service credential redacted.

link_delivery.arguments: message_id required; no local inbox row required
link_delivery.semantics: Read fresh exact GET /v1/messages/{id} delivery_status for the bound sender or explicit recipient in a currently authorized configured channel. Return message/channel/author/recipient IDs and per-recipient native, legacy and qualifying direct-reply facts, never body or session details. Missing delivery_status on an older server returns delivery_status_unavailable; never invent stored or acknowledgement. No seen, acceptance, legacy receipt or SQLite mutation.
link_delivery.status: Convenience precedence replied > accepted > viewed > delivered > offered > stored. All underlying timestamps and legacy uncertainty remain independent. Native provenance is client_reported with server_verified=false. A reply is a same-channel message by that exact recipient, explicitly addressed to the original author with reply_to referencing the original. None of these facts proves execution or completion. Lists and publication receipts omit the detailed aggregate to preserve inbox response bounds.

native_inbox.hook_full_text: Each actually offered hook entry includes full_text:{tool:link_message,arguments:{message_id:<entry id>}} generated from its validated ID. This owned guidance is included before UTF-8 offer-budget accounting and recording inbox.offered, including compact reference_only entries. Hooks validate/regenerate the call; empty or truncated body_preview does not mean an empty message. The hook body remains bounded and untrusted; full reads never implicitly mark seen/accepted.

link_seen.semantics: Explicitly mark viewed, record inbox.seen once across native sessions and suppress default offers. Requires current channel write access and server recipient binding. Does not set accepted_at or change legacy receipts. Repeated call returns replayed=true.

link_accept.semantics: Explicit independent acceptance. Seen messages remain eligible for explicit acceptance. No completion claim or legacy receipt mutation.

native_inbox.status: pending_messages counts all unaccepted messages; unseen_messages counts unaccepted and unseen messages. link_status also reports connector_version/connector_source_commit from the loaded bundle RELEASE.json (connector_identity_source=release_metadata), separately from server_version/server_source_commit from the current authenticated /v1/me.server_build (server_identity_source=authenticated_api). Missing or invalid metadata yields null identity fields and source=unavailable; an unstamped build can report dev with null source commit. Connector identity is captured at module load: restart the MCP process after installing a new bundle. These display stamps are not integrity or authorization proof.
native_inbox.migration: Nullable seen_at/seen_session, persisted integer offer_order and a per-database inbox_view_id are added atomically to old SQLite under BEGIN IMMEDIATE; prior inbox rowids, acceptance, offers, fetch cursors, outbox and binding are preserved. Existing offer timestamps seed the initial global order; new offers increment a logical ordinal. Indexes cover offer history and scheduling. Backend migration extends both native_activity event/message CHECK constraints in place; fair local pagination needs no new backend schema.

native_message_publication.link_send: New messages require nonempty recipient_ids. With reply_to and missing/empty recipients, freshly authorize the configured writable channel, load the exact same-channel parent and resolve its non-self author only. Explicit recipient lists remain unchanged. Names/mentions in body never choose addressees.
native_message_publication.link_broadcast: Explicit channel-only publication: recipient_ids:[] and channel_only:true. No native recipient inbox delivery or model wake. Uses the same durable idempotent outbox and receipt verification.
native_message_publication.compatibility: Legacy directed request hashes unchanged; old queued payloads are never rewritten. New accidental empty sends fail, while exact replay of existing legacy broadcasts remains available. Restart an updated MCP process to load new tools.
native_message_publication.inbox: Sending and status calls do not read inbox. Call link_inbox explicitly; publication success is not recipient viewing.
